card: This pull request decouples the wallet database client version record from CLIENT_VERSION and introduces records tracking the feature flags of the last client to open and decrypt a wallet. It enables future wallet releases to detect upgrade-downgrade-upgrade cycles and safely reapply automatic upgrades without leaving wallets in an inconsistent state. Because this tracking metadata must be present in released versions before any automatic upgrades can safely depend on it, it serves as a prerequisite for future wallet upgrade work, including PR 33034.
changed_since_previous: Added a commit that writes the last opened and decrypted features during legacy wallet migration in ApplyMigrationData, and added logic in LoadWallet to erase stale LAST_DECRYPTED_FEATURES records when loading wallets last modified by versions before VERSION_LAST_CLIENT_FEATURES.
evidence: "When a wallet is automatically upgraded, we always do so in a way that allows the user to load their wallet in an older version. When the user loads their wallet into an upgraded version again, the wallet may not perform the automatic upgrade and end up with upgraded and non-upgraded material in the wallet." (PR description)

"If we write some information about the last client to open the wallet, we would be able to detect these upgrade-downgrade-upgrade situations and perform another upgrade if so. However, in order for this to work, we need to have implemented writing such information into versions prior to the ones which introduce new automatic upgrades." (PR description)
problem: When a wallet undergoes an automatic upgrade and is subsequently opened and modified by an older client version before being loaded again in the newer client, it can end up with a mix of upgraded and non-upgraded material. The wallet has no way to detect upgrade-downgrade-upgrade cycles or determine whether automatic upgrade passes must be reapplied.

risk.why: Mistakes in writing or deleting wallet database records during wallet load or migration could cause database corruption errors and prevent users from loading their wallets.

summary: This pull request decouples the wallet database client version record from CLIENT_VERSION and introduces two database records, LAST_OPENED_FEATURES and LAST_DECRYPTED_FEATURES. These bit flags record the automatic upgrade capabilities of the last client that opened or unlocked and decrypted the wallet file. It also sets these records during legacy wallet migration and discards stale decryption features if loaded from an earlier client version.
